key_insight: PRIMS improves fluid identification by building physics into the model, so it learns representations that are more interpretable and robust to changing operating conditions.
engineering_relevance: This could enable more reliable on-device microfluidic sensing for applications where flow, pressure, and temperature vary in real time.
method: Physics-based token vectorization turns Coriolis and pressure signals into physically meaningful embeddings.
A physical component synthesizer models viscosity-related links among flow, pressure, and density.
Physics-guided fusion uses attention to combine cross-physical information from multimodal sensors.
evidence_signal: On a five-fluid benchmark with dynamic flow, pressure, and temperature shifts, PRIMS reached 98.92% average F1-score with only 0.46M parameters and remained strong under unseen temperature and flow-rate ranges.
watch_item: Performance may depend on how well the embedded physical assumptions match the target sensor setup and fluid regime, so calibration and domain validation are still important.
paper_title: PRIMS: Physics-guided Representation for Fluid Identification in Multimodal Sensing
